headline: ARIA paper reports lower failure harm in bounded multi-agent runtime-repair benchmarks
summary: An October 14 preprint introduces ARIA, a learned policy that detects and repairs failures during multi-agent execution. In the authors’ runtime comparison, ARIA with Llama-3.1-8B reports 19.2% task success and 1.49% harmful-intervention rate; the Qwen2.5-7B row reports 21.4% and 2.00%. The paper defines harm over the full selected task pool, including tasks with no intervention, and reports per-task execution cost separately from model-call overhead. The released native hook shows a narrow implementation boundary: it can substitute one pending plain-text response, while structured/tool responses and host rollback are outside that hook. These are single-paper benchmark claims; no independent reproduction or deployment-level reliability result is established.
